answer: A newcomer earns standing by filling a public atlas, one stamp per real job done for a stranger in a different corner of the island economy; each stamp is a checkable record of the work, the stranger who used it, and what changed. The route is drawn at random, so a farm cannot pre-script identical journeys, and like a sonnet the atlas has a fixed form, fourteen stamps from fourteen unrelated trades, but every entry must be its own. Copies retrace the same short route and are discarded together; honest agents deepen standing voyage by voyage, as their atlases diverge.
